result.title: PBit1: One Programmable P-Bit per Parameter - A Finite-Control Representation of Pretrained Networks
result.comment: 7-page main paper with 3 figures, plus a 12-page supplement
result.summary: We introduce PBit1, a finite-control representation of pretrained neural networks that assigns one programmable p-bit to each learned parameter. A 12-bit command sets its probability, a shared affine range maps that probability to the weight domain, and temporal observations reconstruct the weight for inference. Operator-aware range grouping and sensitivity-based sampling allocation adapt the representation to the network. Across five independent weight draws at 32,768 observations per scalar, selected configurations preserve task quality in GPT-2, DistilBERT, and LFM3-1.7B with every learned scalar converted and no fine-tuning. GPT-2 and LFM3 perplexity increase by approximately 0.66% and 0.26%, respectively, while DistilBERT accuracy changes from 87.51% to 87.49%. A sensitivity-based policy reduces GPT-2 reconstruction observations by 41.7% while retaining the quality criterion. Complete-model evaluations reuse reconstructed weights in BF16 inference, and THRML operator experiments examine native sampling and spatial-temporal tradeoffs. Together, these results establish PBit1 as a concrete construction for studying finite-control weight representation and temporal reconstruction in pretrained networks.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 PBit1，把预训练网络的每个权重映射为一个可编程 p-bit（12 位命令设定概率，共享仿射范围映射到权重域），并用时间上的观测重建权重以供 BF16 推理，在 GPT-2、DistilBERT 和 LFM3-1.7B 上验证无微调下的任务质量保持，并考察基于敏感度的采样分配。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作处理的是静态参数的有损表示与压缩重建，不涉及推理期 latent 视觉状态、证据获取、计算分配或停止决策，也未研究 VLM 推理中的信息保留或使用，缺少可供核查的状态或决策线索，故排除。
